headline: Peace isn't just the absence of conflict—it's the presence of justice, cooperation, and conditions that prevent violence
universal_truth: Sustainable peace is built, not just wished for; it requires addressing root causes
fun_facts: Countries with more trade have fewer wars—economic interdependence creates peace incentives
The longest period of peace between major powers in modern history is happening now
Democracies almost never go to war with each other—a phenomenon called 'democratic peace'
discussion_questions: What's the difference between peace and just 'not fighting right now'?
Where in your life is there surface peace but underlying tension?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The Cold War was 'peace'—no direct fighting. But was it really peaceful? Peace isn't just the absence of violence. It's the presence of justice, opportunity, and conditions that make violence unnecessary. Real peace is positive, not just negative.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often define peace as 'not fighting.' But suppressed conflict can explode. What creates sustainable peace rather than temporary ceasefire?

options.text: Sustainable peace requires addressing root causes—injustice, scarcity, grievances—not just preventing their violent expression
options.response: Yes. Peace built on suppression is fragile. Peace built on addressing underlying needs—justice, opportunity, voice—is resilient. Treat causes, not just symptoms.

options.text: Strong deterrence prevents conflict from erupting
options.response: Deterrence can prevent violence, but true peace requires more than fear of consequences...

q1.title: Positive Peace
q1.script: Scholars distinguish 'negative peace' (absence of violence) from 'positive peace' (presence of justice). A society without war but with oppression isn't truly peaceful. Real peace means people flourish, not just don't fight.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Positive Peace"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Interdependence
q2.script: Countries that trade extensively rarely fight—they have too much to lose. Economic ties create peace incentives. This is why the European Union, born from centuries of war, emphasizes trade. Interdependence is infrastructure for peace.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Peace
q3.script: The same applies personally. Surface calm with underlying resentment isn't peace. Relationships where issues go unaddressed aren't peaceful—they're time bombs. Real peace requires honest engagement with tensions.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Sustainable peace is built, not just wished for. It requires addressing root causes, not just preventing their expression. Build positive peace.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 204. Tomorrow, we'll explore why humans fight—the causes of conflict. Until then, consider where you have negative peace that could become positive peace.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Peace Audit - Surface or Real?
growTrack.activity: Where in your life is there 'negative peace'—no fighting but underlying tension? A relationship, a workplace situation, an internal conflict? What would positive peace require—addressing the root issue, having the honest conversation, creating sustainable resolution?
